architecture: Organize jQuery Commerce Interface into semantic page markup, isolated jQuery behavior functions, and CSS presentation. Keep data fetching and validation boundaries explicit.
implementation_plan: Implement the project objective: Build a responsive storefront whose backend remains the source of truth for product and order data.
Complete milestone: Product listing, search, filters and pagination
Complete milestone: Product details and variants
Complete milestone: Cart quantity changes and removal
Complete milestone: Accessible forms and AJAX operations
Complete milestone: Loading, empty and error recovery
Add loading, empty, error, and success states where applicable.
Write a small regression checklist and verify keyboard/responsive behavior.
Document setup, APIs, dependency versions, security boundaries, and limitations.
reference_code: Use the project starter in projects/starters. The complete solution depends on the learner’s chosen markup, mock/server API, and test environment; review the required behaviors against the rubric rather than treating one code listing as universal.
acceptance_review: All required features can be demonstrated from a fresh page load.
Empty and error states are clear rather than silently failing.
Keyboard users can reach and operate all essential controls.
User/API text is rendered safely; server state and totals are not trusted to the client.
The test matrix records viewport, browser, expected result, actual result, and known gaps.
explanation: This reference plan provides a protected implementation sequence and review standard. It is not a claim that the project has been executed or deployed.
